newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungary MOL signs record gas deal with Panrusgaz.
newsitem.headline: Hungary MOL signs record gas deal with Panrusgaz.

text.p: Hungarian oil and gas company Magyar Olaj- es Gazipari Rt has signed a contract with gas importer Panrusgaz for the delivery of 225 billion cubic metres of Russian natural gas to Hungary over 20 years.

"The terms of the contract are in line with Western European standards," the two companies' joint statement said. Company officials declined to disclose the price of the deal, which covers deliveries up to 2015.
According to MOL figures, Hungary used 11.68 billion cubic metres of natural gas in 1995, of which 6.8 billion was imported, mainly from Russia.
Panrusgaz is a joint venture owned 50-50 percent by MOL and Russia's RAO Gazprom, with a 120 million forints capital.
Lajos Antal, Panrusgaz's deputy general director, told Reuters the deal did not mean earlier plans to sell gas in Hungary direct to the consumer by the end of the century had been abandoned.
"This deal with MOL does not mean that we have renounced those plans," he said.
MOL is Panrusgaz's only customer in Hungary, as only MOL has gas distribution rights in the country.
Since 1975, Hungary has imported over 86 billion cubic metres of gas from Russia, the statement said.
Hungary's natural gas consumption is expected to grow to 15 billion cubic metres per year by 2010, while domestic production would drop to 2.9 billion cubic metres.

The statement also said that deliveries agreed in the present contract are guaranteed by Gazprom and the gas would arrive through the traditional eastern route as well as the recently opened Hungary-Austria (HAG) pipeline.
MOL is 58 percent owned by Hungary's state privatisation agency APV Rt, with foreign investors holding 30 percent.
The second offering of MOL shares for privatisation, expected before the end of the year, has been postponed until 1997 after Hungary delayed an energy price rise expected for October.
The delay is likely to result in MOL losing some 2.5 billion forints on its 1996 gas sales, as they have to pay near market prices on their imports but have to sell at state-controlled rates.
APV officials said earlier the second MOL offering would probably be in the first two months of 1997.
On the Budapest Stock Exchange, MOL shares closed at 1,550 forints, down 20.
